name: Mort (La Morte)
description: Mort (also known as La Morte) is a specialized trick-taking card game for 3 to 5 players, traditionally played with a modified Tarot deck. Created by Matt Haller, it combines the structural depth of Bridge and Tarot with a unique 'Specialist' mechanic centered around the 'La Morte' card (the 13 of Trumps). It involves complex bidding, the ability to 'Drop Out' of a hand to avoid points, and a high penalty for being 'Fuori dal Tempo' (out of time) on the final trick.

history.origins: Designed by Matt Haller as a modern homage to historical Italian Tarot games like Tarocchini, but with simplified bidding and scoring meant for faster play.
timeline: 2000s: Matt Haller documents the rules and distributes them in card gaming circles.
2010s: Becomes a recognized custom Tarot variant in invented-game and card-gaming communities.
Present: Played by enthusiasts of 'Neotraditional' card games.
21st Century: Often cited as an example of how to adapt Tarot mechanics to a standard Western deck.
history.cultural: Regarded as a strategic masterpiece by fans of trick-evaluation games.
history.evolution: The game's 'Il Morto' rule (where a player can be retired from a hand) is a thematic nod to the game's name.

setup.deck: 37 cards (A, K, Q, Cav, J, 10, 9, 8, 7) + 13 of Trumps (La Morte).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 9 cards. The 'Talon' determines the trump suit.

rules.objective: Total the most points through contracts and trick-captures.
rules.gameplay: Each round is 9 tricks. Players must play in the lead suit if possible; otherwise any card may be played. The highest trump in the trick wins, or if no trump was played, the highest card of the led suit wins. The trick winner leads the next trick. La Morte is played as if in the trump suit: players may never lead La Morte unless it is their only card. La Morte wins any trick when trump was led; if led off-trump it loses and the taker becomes Il Morto (scores for that trick but plays no more tricks; lead passes left).
keyRules: Dealer deals 9 cards each; talon sets trump (or no trump if La Morte is talon).
Bid 1 to 9 tricks or all; Accept sets contract; Drop Out aims for 0 tricks.
Follow suit. Highest trump or highest led-suit card wins. La Morte plays as trump; do not lead it unless only card.

Maker makes bid: score contract value; maker fails: each defender scores contract value. Dropper with 0 tricks: contract minus 1; otherwise 0. Each trick worth 1 to maker and defenders. Fuori dal Tempo (lead La Morte on last trick): 0. Revoke: deduct points earned.

strategy.basic: Avoid leading La Morte! Since it loses if led off-trump, it is a defensive card. Use it to kill an opponent's high trump lead. If you are the contract maker, your goal is to draw out the opponents' trumps before they can use La Morte against your high side-suit cards.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Drop Out' Risk: If you have a terrible hand, choice 'Drop Out' in the bidding. Your goal is 0 tricks. This is safer than bidding 1 and failing, as it guarantees you 'Defense' points if the contract maker fails.
strategy.advanced: Timing the Death: Use 'La Morte' to make an opponent 'Il Morto' when they are the strongest. By forcing them to win a non-trump trick with your La Morte, you remove their high cards from the remaining tricks, effectively handing the game to yourself or your partner.
tips: Keep track of the 9 tricks. If you have La Morte, make sure you have at least one other card to lead on the 9th trick to avoid 'Fuori dal Tempo'.
In a 5-player game, 'Il Bagatto' is the highest Club. Treat it like a second 'Super-Trump'.

variations.name: Five players
variations.description: Play with 9 extra cards (two extra ranks per suit) plus Il Bagatto (1 of Trumps), highest Club. Ranks from high: Il Bagatto, A K Q C J 10 9 8 7 6 5.

variations.name: Muck when all drop
variations.description: If all players drop out, dealer may muck the deal (round abandoned, deal passes left) instead of restarting with a bid.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Optional rule only; no engine constant changes required for this variant.

scoring.description: Maker scores contract value if bid made; defenders score contract value if maker fails. Droppers: contract minus 1 if 0 tricks, else 0. Each trick worth 1. Game typically to 50 points or after a set number of deals.
scoring.winCondition: First to reach the target score (typically 50) wins; or highest score after a set number of rounds.
